candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Referrals/Continuity of Care/Collaboration: identify when client findings require specialty referral and coordinate timely access to appropriate interdisciplinary services.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — timely nephrology referral for CKD progression and complications
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize current KDIGO referral triggers for specialist kidney care, including eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities, rather than waiting until dialysis is immediately required.

options.A: Arrange referral to specialist kidney care because both an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities are listed referral circumstances.
options.B: Continue routine primary-care follow-up without referral until dialysis must be started because specialist kidney care is reserved for end-stage kidney failure.
options.C: Avoid referral because electrolyte abnormalities are not considered CKD complications that benefit from specialist management.
options.D: Refer only if the client personally requests a nephrologist because objective kidney-function and complication criteria are not used for referral decisions.

candidate.rationale: KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.1.1 directs referral of adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in the circumstances shown in Figure 48. These include eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium, among several other diagnostic, albuminuria, progression, and complication-related triggers. Early referral supports evaluation, management of CKD complications, and preparation for kidney-replacement therapy when needed. Therefore, A is correct. B waits until kidney failure is too advanced, while C and D ignore explicit objective referral circumstances.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports specialist kidney-care referral for adults with CKD who have eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or persistent serum-potassium abnormalities, well before dialysis is necessarily required.
candidate.source_document_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
candidate.source_locator: Chapter 5, Section 5.1, Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48 (page S255): refer adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in listed circumstances. Figure 48 includes eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium, along with uncertain cause, hereditary kidney disease, significant albuminuria/hematuria, refractory hypertension, acidosis, anemia, bone disease, malnutrition and other triggers.
candidate.source_version_date: 2024; confirmed current global CKD standard in 2026
candidate.stem: An adult with chronic kidney disease has an eGFR of 27 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent hyperkalemia despite appropriate initial management. Which plan is most consistent with current KDIGO guidance?
